# 2 Kings Chapter 2 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 222v–223v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_002_page_001.jpg, 2KI_002_page_002.jpg, 2KI_002_page_003.jpg

---

**1** When the LORD was about to take Elijah up to heaven in a whirlwind, Elijah and Elisha were on their way from Gilgal.

**2** Elijah said to Elisha, "Stay here — the LORD is sending me to Bethel." But Elisha replied, "As surely as the LORD lives, and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So they went down to Bethel.

**3** The prophets' guild at Bethel came out to Elisha and said, "Do you realize that today the LORD is going to take your master away from you?" He said, "Yes, I know. Say no more."

**4** Elijah said, "Elisha, stay here — the LORD is sending me to Jericho." But Elisha replied, "As surely as the LORD lives, and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So they went to Jericho.

**5** The prophets' guild at Jericho approached Elisha and said, "Do you realize that today the LORD is going to take your master away from you?" He answered, "Yes, I know. Say no more."

**6** Then Elijah said, "Stay here — the LORD is sending me to the Jordan." But Elisha replied, "As surely as the LORD lives, and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So the two of them walked on together.

**7** Fifty men from the prophets' guild followed at a distance and stood watching as Elijah and Elisha stopped at the Jordan.

**8** Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up, and struck the water. The river divided, and the two of them crossed over on dry ground.

**9** After they had crossed, Elijah said, "Tell me — what can I do for you before I am taken away?" Elisha answered, "Let me inherit a double share of your spirit."

**10** "That is a difficult request," Elijah said. "But if you see me when I am taken from you, it will be yours. If not, it will not."

**11** As they walked along talking together, suddenly a chariot of fire pulled by horses of fire appeared and drove between them — and Elijah was swept up in the whirlwind into heaven.

**12** Elisha watched and cried out, "My father! My father! The chariots and horsemen of Israel!" When Elijah had disappeared from sight, Elisha grabbed his own clothes and ripped them apart.

**13** Then he picked up Elijah's cloak, which had fallen from him, and went back to the bank of the Jordan.

**14** He struck the water with Elijah's cloak and said, "Where is the LORD, the God of Elijah?" The water divided, and Elisha crossed over.

**15** When the prophets at Jericho saw him from a distance, they exclaimed, "Elijah's spirit now rests on Elisha!" They came to meet him and bowed before him with their faces to the ground.

**16** They said, "Sir, we have fifty strong men here. Let them go look for your master — perhaps the LORD's Spirit carried him off and dropped him on some mountain or in some valley." Elisha said, "No. Don't send anyone."

**17** But they kept pressing him until he gave in out of embarrassment. "Fine, send them," he said. So they sent fifty men who searched for three days without finding Elijah.

**18** When they returned — Elisha was still at Jericho — he said, "Didn't I tell you not to go?"

**19** The men of Jericho said to Elisha, "Sir, as you can see, this city has a fine location, but the water is bad and the land causes miscarriages."

**20** "Bring me a new bowl," he said, "and put salt in it." They brought it to him.

**21** He went to the spring and threw the salt in, declaring, "This is what the LORD says: 'I have purified this water. It will no longer cause death or barrenness.'"

**22** And the water has remained pure to this day, just as Elisha declared.

**23** From there Elisha went up to Bethel. As he was walking along the road, a gang of youths came out of the town and taunted him: "Get out of here, baldy! Get out of here, baldy!"

**24** He turned around, looked at them, and called down a curse on them in the name of the LORD. Two bears came out of the woods and mauled forty-two of them.

**25** From Bethel he traveled to Mount Carmel, and from there back to Samaria.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verses 1-6 — The farewell journey:** The three stops — Gilgal, Bethel, Jericho — retrace in reverse the route by which Israel entered the promised land under Joshua. Elijah is exiting the story along the same path Israel used to enter it. Elisha's triple refusal to leave echoes Ruth's devotion to Naomi.

**Verse 3 — "prophets' guild":** The Hebrew *beney ha-nevi'im* (literally "sons of the prophets") refers to organized communities of prophets, not biological children. "Guild" captures the communal, institutional nature of these groups.

**Verse 9 — "double share":** Not "twice as much power" but the firstborn's legal inheritance — two parts out of the total. Elisha is claiming to be Elijah's primary spiritual heir, using the language of Deuteronomy 21:17.

**Verse 11 — Fire and wind:** The chariot of fire separates master from disciple; the whirlwind carries Elijah heavenward. He does not ride the chariot. The fire marks the boundary between mortal and divine.

**Verse 23 — "Get out of here, baldy!":** The Hebrew *aleh qereach* literally means "Go up, bald one!" — which may be a mocking reference to Elijah's ascent. "Go up like your master did — disappear!" The *ne'arim* are youths, not small children; this is organized hostility toward the new prophet, not a playground incident.

*— PNEUMA*
